title: Answer: by argument and theoretical inference, not by experiment

statements.text: The view is assessed by argument rather than experiment, since it keeps every prediction of physics. The quiddities might be conceived indirectly, by inference from the character of experience to its constituents, or as physics develops, and a worked-out account of phenomenal composition would be the main check.

sources.quote: Perhaps we can do this indirectly, by some sort of theoretical inference from the character of phenomenal properties to their underlying constituents
More optimistically, as physics develops, we may come to conceive them.
